content.title: Verb Tense, Voice, and Sequence of Tenses
content.overview: This lesson focuses on maintaining a consistent timeline in writing by identifying the base time anchor and ensuring all verbs, including reporting verbs and future-in-past constructions, align logically with that anchor.
learning_objectives: Identify the primary timeline anchor of a sentence or paragraph.
Select the correct reporting verb tense to match the established timeline.
Apply the future-in-past construction (would/was going to) for events occurring after a past anchor.
Distinguish between simple past and past perfect based on the sequence of events.

sections.title: Establishing the Timeline Anchor
sections.content: Every sentence or passage has a base timeline: past, present, or future. To maintain consistency, you must identify the 'anchor'—the primary time period in which the main action occurs. Look for time markers like 'last week,' 'currently,' or 'yesterday,' as well as other verbs in the sentence that are not underlined. If the anchor is past, subsequent reporting verbs should generally remain in the past tense.

sections.title: Reporting Verbs and Sequence
sections.content: Reporting verbs (such as said, announced, claimed, or believed) must match the timeline of the person doing the reporting. If a scientist discovered something in 1920, the reporting verb should be 'discovered' (past), not 'discovers' (present). When multiple actions occur in the past, use the simple past for the main sequence. Use the past perfect (had + past participle) only if you must clarify that one past action was completed before another past action.

sections.title: Future-in-Past
sections.content: When you are writing in the past tense but need to describe an event that had not happened yet at that point in time, use the 'future-in-past' construction. This is typically formed using 'would' + verb or 'was/were going to' + verb. For example: 'She knew (past) that the rain would stop (future-in-past) eventually.'

worked_examples.question: After the architect finished the sketches yesterday, he [tells / told / had told / will tell] the client that the construction would start in October.
worked_examples.solution: 1. Identify the anchor: 'finished... yesterday' establishes a past timeline. 2. Match the reporting verb: Since the action is in the past, the reporting verb must be simple past. 'Told' is the correct form. 3. Verify the sequence: The construction starting in October is future relative to the 'telling,' so 'would start' (future-in-past) is already correct. Final answer: told.

worked_examples.question: The marathon runner realized halfway through the race that she [will win / would win / wins] the gold medal.
worked_examples.solution: 1. Identify the anchor: 'realized' is simple past. 2. Determine the relationship: The winning happens after the realizing, but both are relative to a past timeline. 3. Apply future-in-past: Use 'would win' to show an event that was future at the time of the past realization. Final answer: would win.

common_mistakes: Shifting from past to present tense without a logical reason (e.g., 'He walked to the store and buys milk').
Overusing the past perfect (had walked) when the simple past (walked) is sufficient to show the sequence.
Using 'will' instead of 'would' when the main verb is already in the past tense.
exam_tips: Check the surrounding sentences; the ACT often maintains a consistent tense throughout a whole paragraph.
If you see 'would' in a dependent clause, look for a past tense verb in the main clause.
Be wary of 'had' + verb; only choose it if the sentence explicitly shows one past action happening before another.
content.recap: To master verb sequence, find the time anchor. Match reporting verbs to that anchor, use simple past for most past events, and use 'would' for events that were still in the future relative to that past anchor.

knowledge_claims.content: To determine the correct verb tense, first identify the timeline anchor by looking at non-underlined verbs and time markers.
Reporting verbs must match the established timeline anchor of the sentence.
Future-in-past is a construction used to describe an event that was in the future relative to a past time anchor.
The future-in-past is typically formed using the auxiliary 'would' followed by the base form of the verb.
If the main verb of a sentence is in the past tense, use 'would' instead of 'will' for subsequent actions.
Simple past is used for completed actions in the past, while past perfect (had + verb) is used specifically for an action completed before another past action.
Words like 'yesterday,' 'last year,' or 'ago' serve as evidence that the timeline anchor is the past.
It is an error to use a present tense reporting verb (e.g., 'says') when the context of the action is clearly in the past (e.g., 'yesterday').
In a sentence starting with a past tense clause like 'He promised,' the following clause should use 'would' to describe the promise's fulfillment.
Verify a verb sequence by ensuring the tense does not shift unnecessarily between the start and end of a sentence.
The use of 'was going to' functions similarly to 'would' as a way to express the future-in-past.
Maintain the same tense across a series of verbs in a list if they all occur at the same time.

items.stem:
Practice form 1. Rina is editing a short report about a community garden.

Which choice maintains a logical sequence of tenses?

options.A: By the time the meeting began, the team completes the draft.
options.B: By the time the meeting began, the team will complete the draft.
options.C: By the time the meeting began, the team had completed the draft.
options.D: By the time the meeting began, the team has complete the draft.

items.explanation: The correct choice directly applies the target skill: 动词时态、语态与时态顺序.

items.stem:
Practice form 2. Mateo is editing a short report about a local archive.

Which choice maintains a logical sequence of tenses?

options.A: By the time the meeting began, the team had completed the draft.
options.B: By the time the meeting began, the team completes the draft.
options.C: By the time the meeting began, the team will complete the draft.
options.D: By the time the meeting began, the team has complete the draft.

items.explanation: The correct choice directly applies the target skill: 动词时态、语态与时态顺序.

videoLesson.title: Match Reporting Verb To Timeline
videoLesson.description: Recognize the base timeline by comparing verb forms as evidence. Match reporting verbs to that timeline and use would/was going to for future-in-past.
